stem: If \(x\) and \(y\) are integers such that \(x + y = 20\) and \(3x - 2y > 30\), what is the least possible value of \(x\)?
solution: The inequality is strict, so \(x = 14\) fails (\(42 - 12 = 30\), not greater than 30). The least integer value is \(x = 15\).
verify:
x = symbols('x')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(3*x - 2*(20 - x) > 30, x, relational=False)
assert s == Interval.open(14, oo)
least = min(k for k in range(-50, 100) if k in s)
assert least == 15 and [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [least]
